narrative.overview:
Dakdot is an ink-black studio page with one character on it. The dot in the wordmark is alive: a large paper disc with ink eyes that leans toward the pointer on a spring, squashes and stretches with its speed, blinks, boings when poked, and on scroll travels up to dock into the header logo, where it becomes the logo's dot again. Everything else on the page is quiet so that Dot and the type can be loud: a monochrome ink ground, paper text, one heavy grotesk set very large and very tight, and generous dark space between sections.

Colour is not an accent here. It arrives only as whole fields, one per service: Web Development is flooded brand red, Motion is flooded yellow, Brand Design stays neutral as a paper field with ink text. Outside those fields the page is ink, paper and grey, with the single exception of the red action fill on the primary button. Motion is rich but quick, and it never costs content: every heading and block is visible before JavaScript runs, reveals arm only for content still below the fold, and reduced motion or `?still` gives a still Dot and a still page.

The client rejected the previous direction for scattering colour and for its transit-line and route-map vocabulary. Thin hairline dividers remain part of this world (the work list and footer use them); route rails, line-coloured strokes and station metaphors do not.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome ink ground (ink) with paper text and mute grey secondary copy.
Colour only as whole-section fields with their own paired text colour.
One family, Schibsted Grotesk, headings at 800 with tight negative tracking.
Pill buttons with a rolling label, a rotating arrow and a magnetic pull.
A contextual cursor badge that names the action under the pointer.
Split-word and scroll reveals that arm only below the fold.
Dot, the living logo dot, as the brand character.

rules.name: The Field Rule
rules.body: Colour lives on whole sections, never as scattered accents. A service gets its colour as a full rounded field with its paired text colour (`--color-field-*` / `--color-on-*`); text, borders, icons and decorations on ink stay ink, paper or grey. The only colours permitted outside a field are the signal fill on the primary action, the yellow focus ring, error red on form errors, and the WhatsApp mark's own green.

rules.name: The Paired Text Rule
rules.body: Inside a field, every element (title, copy, chips, arrow circle, focus outline) is drawn in that field's `--color-on-*` colour or its inverse. Never place paper text on the Design or Motion fields, or ink text on the Development field.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: One family, Schibsted Grotesk, at every level. Hierarchy comes from size, weight 800 versus 400, and tracking, never from a second typeface.

rules.name: The Tight Slab Rule
rules.body: Any heading at headline size or above uses weight 800, negative tracking of at least -0.035em, and line height at or below 1.

rules.name: The Flat Field Rule
rules.body: Fields, buttons, chips and cards carry no shadow. Only something that physically follows the pointer above the page may cast one.

rules.name: The One Dot Rule
rules.body: Dot appears once per page as the hero character, and otherwise only inside the wordmark (header logo, footer mark). Never duplicate it, recolour it, or give it a mouth, limbs or a costume; it is a paper disc with two ink eyes.

rules.name: The Dot Lives on Ink Rule
rules.body: Dot's difference blend is tuned for ink and paper. Keep it over the ink ground, not over a colour field.

rules.name: The Visible-First Rule
rules.body: Motion never hides content that would otherwise be seen. Hero lines are visible from the first frame and only settle upward (from 0.35 opacity, 0.25em). `reveal` and `splitWords` arm only elements still below 90% of the viewport when JavaScript runs; above-the-fold content and no-JS content are never hidden.

rules.name: The Stand-Down Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, or when the URL carries `?still`, every motion action stands down: no magnetic pull, no reveals or split words, no rolling headline word, and Dot stays a still dot with open eyes in the hero. Reduced motion additionally skips Lenis smooth scrolling, the hero line settle, the footer eyes, CSS label rolls and the cursor badge's lag. New motion gates on `stillMode()` so both signals are honoured. Static captures of the page are taken with `?still`.

dos: **Do** put colour on whole sections only: a 24px-radius field in `--color-field-dev`, `--color-field-design` or `--color-field-motion`, with all its contents in the matching `--color-on-*`.
**Do** keep every section inside the 88rem container with the 1.5rem gutter so edges align with the header.
**Do** use RollButton for every button and pill link; Primary for the main action, Light in the header, Ghost for secondary actions on ink, Ink on paper or yellow fields.
**Do** give interactive elements a short `data-cursor` label that names the action.
**Do** set headings in Schibsted Grotesk 800 with negative tracking (-0.035em to -0.045em) and line height at or below 1.
**Do** reveal with `use:reveal` and `use:splitWords` from `$lib/actions/motion`, and gate any new motion on `stillMode()`.
**Do** use 1px hairlines (rule) to divide lists, and Hairline Strong (rule-strong) to outline interactive things at rest.
**Do** use the paper field for confirmation and quiet emphasis panels on ink.
donts: **Don't** scatter colour as accents: no coloured headings, coloured borders, coloured icons or coloured tags on the ink ground.
**Don't** bring back the rejected transit vocabulary: route rails, line-coloured strokes, station dots or network maps.
**Don't** add a second typeface, or set large headings at lighter weights.
**Don't** add shadows to fields, buttons or cards; the only shadow is the floating preview's.
**Don't** hide content behind motion: never start above-the-fold content at opacity 0, and never let a reveal run when `stillMode()` is true.
**Don't** add a second living character or alter Dot's form.
**Don't** use WhatsApp green anywhere except inside the WhatsApp mark.
